evidence: src/products/application/use-cases/delete-product/delete-product.command-handler.ts: execute() runs `throw new NotFoundException(`Product with id ${productId} not found`)`. NotFoundException is the NestJS HTTP 404 exception, so this is transport/presentation (infrastructure) logic.
import { NotFoundException } from '@nestjs/common' brings an HTTP-transport exception type into an application use case.
Orchestration (`productRepository.exists` then `productRepository.delete`) is a proper application-layer responsibility.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of DeleteProductCommandHandler does application-layer work. It handles a command, checks whether the product exists and asks the repository to delete it. One part belongs to a different layer. When the product is missing, execute() throws NotFoundException from @nestjs/common. This is an HttpException subclass that carries an HTTP 404 status and response body, so the use case is choosing the HTTP response itself. Mapping errors to HTTP is a transport/presentation concern, which this layer model files under infrastructure (controllers / exception filters). The application layer should throw an application or domain error such as ProductNotFoundError and let the presentation layer turn it into a 404. The handler also imports a concrete infrastructure ProductRepository. That is an import-direction issue, which is out of scope and was not counted here. Confidence is moderate because many NestJS codebases accept HTTP exceptions in their handlers.
